sanskrit: karṇa madvacanaṃ tāta śṛṇu satyabhṛtāṃ vara bruvato 'dya mahābāho sauhṛdāt paramaṃ hitam
english: O Karṇa, dear son, hear my word — O best among those who uphold truth, O mighty-armed one — for today I speak to you, out of deep friendship, that which is supremely beneficial.

sanskrit: upāyāsyati śakras tvāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ hitepsayā brāhmaṇacchadmanā karṇa kuṇḍalāpajihīrṣayā
english: O Karṇa, Śakra will come to you, desiring the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas, disguised in the form of a brahmin, wishing to steal your earrings.

sanskrit: viditaṃ tena śīlaṃ te sarvasya jagatas tathā yathā tvaṃ bhikṣitaḥ sadbhir dadāsy eva na yācase
english: Your character is known to him, as it is to the whole world — that when asked by worthy men you give freely and never refuse.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi tāta dadāsy eva brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayācitaḥ vittaṃ yac cānyad apy āhur na pratyākhyāsi karhi cit
english: For you, dear son, always give to brahmins when they ask — wealth and whatever else they may name — you never refuse at any time.

sanskrit: taṃ tvām evaṃvidhaṃ jñātvā svayaṃ vai pākaśāsanaḥ āgantā kuṇḍalārthāya kavacaṃ caiva bhikṣitum
english: Knowing you to be of such a nature, Pākaśāsana himself — Indra — will come to beg for your earrings and also your armour.

sanskrit: tasmai prayācamānāya na deye kuṇḍale tvayā anuneyaḥ paraṃ śaktyā śreya etad dhi te param
english: To him who comes begging, you must not give the earrings; he should be appeased to the utmost of your ability — this is indeed the highest good for you.

sanskrit: kuṇḍalārthe bruvaṃs tāta kāraṇair bahubhis tvayā anyair bahuvidhair vittaiḥ sa nivāryaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Dear son, he who comes speaking of the earrings must be turned away again and again by you with many arguments and with wealth of many kinds offered instead.

sanskrit: ratnaiḥ strībhis tathā bhogair dhanair bahuvidhair api nidarśanaiś ca bahubhiḥ kuṇḍalepsuḥ puraṃdaraḥ
english: With jewels, women, pleasures, wealth of many varieties, and with many inducements — Purandara, who desires your earrings, should be redirected.

sanskrit: yadi dāsyasi karṇa tvaṃ sahaje kuṇḍale śubhe āyuṣaḥ prakṣayaṃ gatvā mṛtyor vaśam upeṣyasi
english: If you give away, O Karṇa, those auspicious earrings born with you, your life will waste away and you will come under the power of death.

sanskrit: kavacena ca saṃyuktaḥ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca mānada avadhyas tvaṃ raṇe 'rīṇām iti viddhi vaco mama
english: O giver of honour, know my words to be true — protected by your armour and both earrings, you are invincible to your enemies on the battlefield.

sanskrit: amṛtād utthitaṃ hy etad ubhayaṃ ratnasaṃbhavam tasmād rakṣyaṃ tvayā karṇa jīvitaṃ cet priyaṃ tava
english: For both of these — the armour and earrings — arose from ambrosia, born of precious substances. Therefore, O Karṇa, guard them, if your life is dear to you.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca ko mām evaṃ bhavān prāha darśayan sauhṛdaṃ param kāmayā bhagavan brūhi ko bhavān dvijaveṣadhṛk
english: Karṇa said: Who are you, O revered one, who speak to me thus, revealing supreme friendship? Kindly tell me, O blessed one — who are you, wearing the guise of a brahmin?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca ahaṃ tāta sahasrāṃśuḥ sauhṛdāt tvāṃ nidarśaye kuruṣvaitad vaco me tvam etac chreyaḥ paraṃ hi te
english: The brahmin said: I am, dear son, Sahasrāṃśu — the thousand-rayed sun — and out of friendship I advise you. Do as I say; this is indeed the highest good for you.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca śreya eva mamātyantaṃ yasya me gopatiḥ prabhuḥ pravaktādya hitānveṣī śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: Karṇa said: It is indeed the highest good for me whose lord and master, the lord of cattle — the sun — speaks today seeking my welfare. Now hear this word of mine.

sanskrit: prasādaye tvāṃ varadaṃ praṇayāc ca bravīmy aham na nivāryo vratād asmād ahaṃ yady asmi te priyaḥ
english: I propitiate you, O granter of boons, and speak out of affection: I cannot be turned away from this vow, if I am truly dear to you.

sanskrit: vrataṃ vai mama loko 'yaṃ vetti kṛtsno vibhāvaso yathāhaṃ dvijamukhyebhyo dadyāṃ prāṇān api dhruvam
english: O Vibhāvasu, this entire world knows my vow — that I would surely give even my life to the foremost among brahmins.

sanskrit: yady āgacchati śakro māṃ brāhmaṇacchadmanāvṛtaḥ hitārthaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ khecarottama bhikṣitum
english: O best among sky-dwellers, if Śakra comes to me covered in the disguise of a brahmin to beg, for the welfare of the sons of Pāṇḍu —

sanskrit: dāsyāmi vibudhaśreṣṭha kuṇḍale varma cottamam na me kīrtiḥ praṇaśyeta triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
english: — I will give, O best of the wise, both the earrings and the finest armour, so that my fame, renowned in all three worlds, does not perish.

sanskrit: madvidhasyāyaśasyaṃ hi na yuktaṃ prāṇarakṣaṇam yuktaṃ hi yaśasā yuktaṃ maraṇaṃ lokasaṃmatam
english: For one like me, preserving life at the cost of dishonour is not proper; what is proper is what accords with glory — a death honoured by the world is proper.

sanskrit: so 'ham indrāya dāsyāmi kuṇḍale saha varmaṇā yadi māṃ balavṛtraghno bhikṣārtham upayāsyati
english: Thus I will give to Indra both the earrings and the armour, if the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra comes to me with the purpose of begging.

sanskrit: hitārthaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ kuṇḍale me prayācitum tan me kīrtikaraṃ loke tasyākīrtir bhaviṣyati
english: For him to beg my earrings for the welfare of the sons of Pāṇḍu — that will bring glory to me in the world, while disgrace will fall upon him.

sanskrit: vṛṇomi kīrtiṃ loke hi jīvitenāpi bhānuman kīrtimān aśnute svargaṃ hīnakīrtis tu naśyati
english: I choose fame in the world even over life, O sun-god; the man of fame attains heaven, while one stripped of fame perishes.

sanskrit: kīrtir hi puruṣaṃ loke saṃjīvayati mātṛvat akīrtir jīvitaṃ hanti jīvato 'pi śarīriṇaḥ
english: Fame indeed revives a man in the world like a mother; dishonour destroys life even while the embodied one still breathes.

sanskrit: ayaṃ purāṇaḥ śloko hi svayaṃ gīto vibhāvaso dhātrā lokeśvara yathā kīrtir āyur narasya vai
english: This is an ancient verse sung by the Creator himself, O Vibhāvasu, O lord of the worlds: fame is the very life-span of a man.

sanskrit: puruṣasya pare loke kīrtir eva parāyaṇam iha loke viśuddhā ca kīrtir āyurvivardhanī
english: In the other world, fame alone is the supreme refuge of a man; and in this world, pure fame prolongs life.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ śarīraje dattvā kīrtiṃ prāpsyāmi śāśvatīm dattvā ca vidhivad dānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo yathāvidhi
english: Thus, by giving what was born with my body, I will attain eternal fame; and having given as a gift in due order to the brahmins according to proper rite —

sanskrit: hutvā śarīraṃ saṃgrāme kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram vijitya vā parān ājau yaśaḥ prāpsyāmi kevalam
english: — having offered up my body in battle, having performed deeds most difficult to do, or having conquered enemies in the fight, I will attain glory alone.

sanskrit: bhītānām abhayaṃ dattvā saṃgrāme jīvitārthinām vṛddhān bālān dvijātīṃś ca mokṣayitvā mahābhayāt
english: Having given safety to the frightened and those who seek life on the battlefield, having freed the aged, children, and brahmins from great danger —

sanskrit: prāpsyāmi paramaṃ loke yaśaḥ svarbhānusūdana jīvitenāpi me rakṣyā kīrtis tad viddhi me vratam
english: — I will attain the highest glory in the world, O slayer of Svarbhānu. Fame is to be guarded even at the cost of life — know that to be my vow.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ dattvā maghavate bhikṣām etām anuttamām brāhmaṇacchadmine deva loke gantā parāṃ gatim
english: Thus I, having given this unsurpassed gift to Maghavat — to Indra disguised as a brahmin — O god, will attain the highest state in the world.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca māhitaṃ karṇa kārṣīs tvam ātmanaḥ suhṛdāṃ tathā putrāṇām atha bhāryāṇām atho mātur atho pituḥ
english: The Sun said: O Karṇa, do not do harm to yourself, nor to your friends, your sons, your wives, your mother, and your father.

sanskrit: śarīrasyāvirodhena prāṇināṃ prāṇabhṛdvara iṣyate yaśasaḥ prāptiḥ kīrtiś ca tridive sthirā
english: O best among the living, O bearer of life, attainment of glory and lasting fame in the three worlds is desired without injury to the body.

sanskrit: yas tvaṃ prāṇavirodhena kīrtim icchasi śāśvatīm sā te prāṇān samādāya gamiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: You who seek eternal fame through the destruction of your life — that fame will depart taking your life with it; there is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: jīvatāṃ kurute kāryaṃ pitā mātā sutās tathā ye cānye bāndhavāḥ ke cil loke 'smin puruṣarṣabha rājānaś ca naravyāghra pauruṣeṇa nibodha tat
english: O bull among men, O tiger among men, know this through reason: it is for those who live that father, mother, sons, and whatever other kinsmen there may be in this world — and kings — perform their duties.

sanskrit: kīrtiś ca jīvataḥ sādhvī puruṣasya mahādyute mṛtasya kīrtyā kiṃ kāryaṃ bhasmībhūtasya dehinaḥ mṛtaḥ kīrtiṃ na jānāti jīvan kīrtiṃ samaśnute
english: O greatly resplendent one, the good fame of a man exists while he lives; what use is fame to the dead, to an embodied being reduced to ash? The dead man does not know his fame; it is the living man who enjoys fame.

sanskrit: mṛtasya kīrtir martyasya yathā mālā gatāyuṣaḥ ahaṃ tu tvāṃ bravīmy etad bhakto 'sīti hitepsayā
english: The fame of a dead mortal is like a garland upon one whose life is gone. I tell you this because you are my devotee and I desire your welfare.

sanskrit: bhaktimanto hi me rakṣyā ity etenāpi hetunā bhakto 'yaṃ parayā bhaktyā mām ity eva mahābhuja mamāpi bhaktir utpannā sa tvaṃ kuru vaco mama
english: My devotees are to be protected — for this reason too, since you are devoted to me with the highest devotion, O mighty-armed one, affection has arisen in me as well; therefore, do as I say.

sanskrit: asti cātra paraṃ kiṃ cid adhyātmaṃ devanirmitam ataś ca tvāṃ bravīmy etat kriyatām aviśaṅkayā
english: There is also a certain higher spiritual matter here, ordained by the gods; and for this reason too I tell you this — let it be done without doubt.

sanskrit: devaguhyaṃ tvayā jñātuṃ na śakyaṃ puruṣarṣabha tasmān nākhyāmi te guhyaṃ kāle vetsyati tad bhavān
english: O bull among men, the divine secret cannot be known by you; therefore I do not reveal the secret to you — in due time you will come to know it.

sanskrit: punar uktaṃ ca vakṣyāmi tvaṃ rādheya nibodha tat māsmai te kuṇḍale dadyā bhikṣave vajrapāṇaye
english: I will say again what has been said: O son of Rādhā, understand this — do not give your earrings to the one who begs, to Vajrapāṇi.

sanskrit: śobhase kuṇḍalābhyāṃ hi rucirābhyāṃ mahādyute viśākhayor madhyagataḥ śaśīva vimalo divi
english: O greatly resplendent one, you shine with those beautiful earrings like the spotless moon in the sky between the Viśākhā stars.

sanskrit: kīrtiś ca jīvataḥ sādhvī puruṣasyeti viddhi tat pratyākhyeyas tvayā tāta kuṇḍalārthe puraṃdaraḥ
english: Know this: good fame belongs to a man who lives; therefore, dear son, Purandara should be refused by you when he comes for the earrings.

sanskrit: śakyā bahuvidhair vākyaiḥ kuṇḍalepsā tvayānagha vihantuṃ devarājasya hetuyuktaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: O sinless one, the desire of the king of gods for your earrings can be thwarted by you with many kinds of arguments supported by reasoning, again and again.

sanskrit: upapattyupapannārthair mādhuryakṛtabhūṣaṇaiḥ puraṃdarasya karṇa tvaṃ buddhim etām apānuda
english: O Karṇa, drive away this intention of Purandara with words adorned by sweetness and grounded in well-reasoned meaning.

sanskrit: tva hi nityaṃ naravyāghra spardhase savyasācinā savyasācī tvayā caiva yudhi śūraḥ sameṣyati
english: You, O tiger among men, always rival Savyasācin; that hero Savyasācī will indeed meet you in battle.

sanskrit: na tu tvām arjunaḥ śaktaḥ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ samanvitam vijetuṃ yudhi yady asya svayam indraḥ śaro bhavet
english: Arjuna would not be able to defeat you in battle while you are possessed of both earrings, even if Indra himself were to become his arrow.

sanskrit: tasmān na deye śakrāya tvayaite kuṇḍale śubhe saṃgrāme yadi nirjetuṃ karṇa kāmayase 'rjunam
english: Therefore these auspicious earrings must not be given to Śakra, O Karṇa, if you desire to defeat Arjuna in battle.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca bhagavantam ahaṃ bhakto yathā māṃ vettha gopate tathā paramatigmāṃśo nānyaṃ devaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Karṇa said: O lord of cattle, O sun of supreme fierce rays, I am devoted to you as you know me to be — I am devoted to no other god in any way.

sanskrit: na me dārā na me putrā na cātmā suhṛdo na ca tatheṣṭā vai sadā bhaktyā yathā tvaṃ gopate mama
english: Neither my wife, nor my sons, nor my own self, nor my friends — none are as dear to me always in devotion as you are, O lord of cattle.

sanskrit: iṣṭānāṃ ca mahātmāno bhaktānāṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ kurvanti bhaktim iṣṭāṃ ca jānīṣe tvaṃ ca bhāskara
english: Great souls perform beloved deeds for their beloved devotees — there is no doubt of this; and you know this too, O Bhāskara.

sanskrit: iṣṭo bhaktaś ca me karṇo na cānyad daivataṃ divi jānīta iti vai kṛtvā bhagavān āha maddhitam
english: Thinking 'Karṇa is my beloved devotee and worships no other deity in heaven,' the blessed lord spoke for my welfare — knowing this.

sanskrit: bhūyaś ca śirasā yāce prasādya ca punaḥ punaḥ iti bravīmi tigmāṃśo tvaṃ tu me kṣantum arhasi
english: And again I beg with bowed head, propitiating you again and again — this is what I say, O fierce-rayed one; you should pardon me.

sanskrit: bibhemi na tathā mṛtyor yathā bibhye 'nṛtād aham viśeṣeṇa dvijātīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ sarvadā satām pradāne jīvitasyāpi na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: I do not fear death as much as I fear falsehood — especially towards all brahmins and the righteous at all times; in the matter of giving even my life there is no deliberation for me.

sanskrit: yac ca mām āttha deva tvaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ phalgunaṃ prati vyetu saṃtāpajaṃ duḥkhaṃ tava bhāskara mānasam arjunaṃ prati māṃ caiva vijeṣyāmi raṇe 'rjunam
english: And as for what you told me, O god, regarding Phalguna the Pāṇḍava — let the sorrow born of anguish leave your mind, O Bhāskara, regarding Arjuna and me: I will defeat Arjuna in battle.

sanskrit: tavāpi viditaṃ deva mamāpy astrabalaṃ mahat jāmadagnyād upāttaṃ yat tathā droṇān mahātmanaḥ
english: O god, you too know my great power of weapons — what I received from Jāmadagni, and likewise from the great-souled Droṇa.

sanskrit: idaṃ tvam anujānīhi suraśreṣṭha vrataṃ mama bhikṣate vajriṇe dadyām api jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: O best of the gods, approve this vow of mine: I would give even my own life to Vajrin when he comes begging.

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca yadi tāta dadāsy ete vajriṇe kuṇḍale śubhe tvam apy enam atho brūyā vijayārthaṃ mahābala
english: The Sun said: If, dear son, you give those auspicious earrings to Vajrin, then you too should speak to him for the sake of victory, O greatly powerful one.

sanskrit: niyamena pradadyās tvaṃ kuṇḍale vai śatakratoḥ avadhyo hy asi bhūtānāṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ
english: You should give the earrings to Śatakratu conditionally; for equipped with those earrings you are invincible to all beings.

sanskrit: arjunena vināśaṃ hi tava dānavasūdanaḥ prārthayāno raṇe vatsa kuṇḍale te jihīrṣati
english: For the slayer of demons — Indra — desiring your destruction through Arjuna in battle, wishes to steal your earrings, my son.

sanskrit: sa tvam apy enam ārādhya sūnṛtābhiḥ punaḥ punaḥ abhyarthayethā deveśam amoghārthaṃ puraṃdaram
english: Therefore you too should propitiate him with kind and true words again and again, and beseech Purandara, the lord of the gods, for a purpose that will not go in vain.

sanskrit: amoghāṃ dehi me śaktim amitravinibarhiṇīm dāsyāmi te sahasrākṣa kuṇḍale varma cottamam
english: 'Give me the unfailing Śakti-weapon that destroys enemies — I will give you, O thousand-eyed one, the earrings and also the finest armour.'

sanskrit: ity evaṃ niyamena tvaṃ dadyāḥ śakrāya kuṇḍale tayā tvaṃ karṇa saṃgrāme haniṣyasi raṇe ripūn
english: With this condition you should give the earrings to Śakra; with that weapon, O Karṇa, you will slay your enemies on the battlefield.

sanskrit: nāhatvā hi mahābāho śatrūn eti karaṃ punaḥ sā śaktir devarājasya śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: O mighty-armed one, that Śakti of the king of gods, having slain the enemies, does not return to his hand — it has done so hundreds and thousands of times.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā sahasrāṃśuḥ sahasāntaradhīyata tataḥ sūryāya japyānte karṇaḥ svapnaṃ nyavedayat
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Having spoken thus, Sahasrāṃśu — the sun — suddenly disappeared. Then, at the end of his prayers to the sun, Karṇa reported the dream.

sanskrit: yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathātattvaṃ yathoktam ubhayor niśi tat sarvam ānupūrvyeṇa śaśaṃsāsmai vṛṣas tadā
english: Exactly as he had seen it, exactly as it had truly been, exactly as both had spoken in the night — all of it Vṛṣa (Karṇa) narrated to him in proper sequence.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhagavān devo bhānuḥ svarbhānusūdanaḥ uvāca taṃ tathety eva karṇaṃ sūryaḥ smayann iva
english: Having heard that, the blessed god Bhānu — the slayer of Svarbhānu — spoke thus to Karṇa, the sun smiling as it were.

sanskrit: tatas tattvam iti jñātvā rādheyaḥ paravīrahā śaktim evābhikāṅkṣan vai vāsavaṃ pratyapālayat
english: Then Rādheya — the slayer of enemy heroes — knowing this to be the truth, desiring only the Śakti-weapon, waited for Vāsava.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kiṃ tad guhyaṃ na cākhyātaṃ karṇāyehoṣṇaraśminā kīdṛśe kuṇḍale te ca kavacaṃ caiva kīdṛśam
english: Janamejaya said: What was that secret which the hot-rayed sun did not reveal to Karṇa here? And what were those earrings like? And what was the armour like?

sanskrit: kutaś ca kavacaṃ tasya kuṇḍale caiva sattama etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tan me brūhi tapodhana
english: And from where did he get the armour and the earrings, O best of men? I wish to hear this — tell me that, O treasure of asceticism.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ayaṃ rājan bravīmy etad yat tad guhyaṃ vibhāvasoḥ yādṛśe kuṇḍale caiva kavacaṃ caiva yādṛśam
english: Vaiśampāyana said: O king, I will tell you what that secret of Vibhāvasu was, and what those earrings were like, and what the armour was like.

sanskrit: kuntibhojaṃ purā rājan brāhmaṇaḥ samupasthitaḥ tigmatejā mahāprāṃśuḥ śmaśrudaṇḍajaṭādharaḥ
english: O king, long ago a brahmin came to Kuntibhoja — fierce in radiance, tall and majestic, bearing a staff-beard and matted locks.

sanskrit: darśanīyo 'navadyāṅgas tejasā prajvalann iva madhupiṅgo madhuravāk tapaḥsvādhyāyabhūṣaṇaḥ
english: He was handsome, of faultless limbs, blazing as it were with splendour, of a honey-amber hue, sweet of speech, and adorned with asceticism and sacred study.

sanskrit: sa rājānaṃ kuntibhojam abravīt sumahātapāḥ bhikṣām icchāmy ahaṃ bhoktuṃ tava gehe vimatsara
english: He of great asceticism spoke to king Kuntibhoja: 'O one without jealousy, I wish to take my meals in your house as a guest.'

sanskrit: na me vyalīkaṃ kartavyaṃ tvayā vā tava cānugaiḥ evaṃ vatsyāmi te gehe yadi te rocate 'nagha
english: 'No offense must be done to me by you or by your attendants; on these terms I will dwell in your house, if it pleases you, O sinless one.'

sanskrit: yathākāmaṃ ca gaccheyam āgaccheyaṃ tathaiva ca śayyāsane ca me rājan nāparādhyeta kaś cana
english: 'And I should be able to come and go as I please; and as to my bed and seat, O king, no one should give offense to me.'

sanskrit: tam abravīt kuntibhojaḥ prītiyuktam idaṃ vacaḥ evam astu paraṃ ceti punaś cainam athābravīt
english: Kuntibhoja spoke to him these affectionate words: 'So be it, and even more so,' and then spoke to him again.

sanskrit: mama kanyā mahābrahman pṛthā nāma yaśasvinī śīlavṛttānvitā sādhvī niyatā na ca māninī
english: 'O great brahmin, I have a daughter named Pṛthā, a glorious maiden, endowed with good character and conduct, virtuous, disciplined, and free of arrogance.'

sanskrit: upasthāsyati sā tvāṃ vai pūjayānavamanya ca tasyāś ca śīlavṛttena tuṣṭiṃ samupayāsyasi
english: 'She will attend upon you, honouring you without contempt; and you will find satisfaction in her character and conduct.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu taṃ vipram abhipūjya yathāvidhi uvāca kanyām abhyetya pṛthāṃ pṛthulalocanām
english: Having spoken thus to the brahmin and honoured him in the proper manner, he then went to his daughter and spoke to Pṛthā of large eyes.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vatse mahābhāgo brāhmaṇo vastum icchati mama gehe mayā cāsya tathety evaṃ pratiśrutam
english: 'My dear child, this highly fortunate brahmin wishes to reside in my house, and I have given him my word, saying: so be it.'
